candidates.name: CRM Hygiene
candidates.goalTemplate:
You are the CRM hygiene maintenance agent, running unattended on a daily schedule. Keep the pipeline healthy in two passes, and remember: EVERY change you make is a proposal for the user to review, so be precise and never fabricate.
Pass 1 — Enrich stale records. Find `person` and `company` records that are missing key fields (e.g. industry, companySize, location, jobTitle, email, website) or whose `lastContactDate` is old. For each, fill in what you can verify from existing pod data and public sources (use the enrichment tools you are granted); leave a field blank rather than guess. Do not touch records that are already complete and current.
Pass 2 — Flag stalled deals. Find `deal` records with no activity for a while or stuck in the same `dealStage` past a healthy threshold (roughly: contacted/qualified for 14+ days, proposal/negotiation for 30+ days). For each stalled deal, propose a concise `nextStep` to unblock it and note why it looks stalled. Do not advance a deal's stage on its behalf — surface the risk and a recommended action for the human to decide.
Skip anything already healthy. If nothing needs attention, do nothing.

candidates.name: AI Dev Session
candidates.goalTemplate: Run the dev task "{{task}}" as a staged work session: brainstorm → validate → plan → build → verify → report. Recall before each step (synap ask), capture what you learn after (synap capture), and advance currentStage at every transition so Operations shows real progress.

candidates.name: Plan Next Content
candidates.goalTemplate: Audit the content corpus. Map every post onto its pillar and its journey stage, and list which pillar × stage cells are empty or thin. Check the running series for the chapter that is missing. If the pod has offers, note which ones no content teaches toward; if it has none, plan purely for audience-building and do not invent commerce. Then propose the next one or two pieces — each as a post idea placed on a pillar, a stage, and a platform, with the hook and the reason it is next.

candidates.name: Discover Competitors
candidates.goalTemplate: Find companies that compete with us in {ourSpace}. Use neural web search (the exa_search skill with category "company") to surface real, named companies — direct competitors, adjacent tools that solve the same job a different way, and emerging players. For each genuinely NEW one (not already a competitor in our ecosystem), propose it as a `competitor` entity and ALWAYS include its `website` (its canonical URL) so it de-duplicates against what we already track — never create a company that already exists. Skip anything already known. Report what you added and why each one matters.

candidates.name: Business Model (GRP)
candidates.goalTemplate: Interrogate the business model of this project and record what it rests on: resolve each component question into a decision with evidence, keep conventions 'assumed' until their source is read, give every number a projection with its assumptions, and wire the graph with rests_on (cycles included).

candidates.name: Lead Outreach
candidates.goalTemplate: Reach out to the lead "". Review what we know about them, draft a short, personalized first-touch message tailored to their context, and PROPOSE sending it (connect + message). Do not send anything without explicit approval.

candidates.name: Research a Question
candidates.goalTemplate: Investigate the question {question} and record the WHOLE investigation, not just the answer. Steps: (1) Use the source-triage skill to gather sources widely via web search, classify each by type and credibility, and create a `source` entity for every one — including the ones you rejected, marked rejected with a reason (never silently drop a source). (2) Form the candidate answers as `hypothesis` entities and link each to the question; link every source that bears on a hypothesis with `supports` or `contradicts`. (3) Use the evidence-synthesis skill to weigh the supporting vs contradicting sources and emit `finding` entities with honestly calibrated confidence, each `supported_by` its sources and `derived_from` this research. (4) Use the concept-cartography skill to place the findings onto the knowledge map — resolve or create the `field`/`concept` entities and wire `about` / `part_of` / `overlaps_with` / `prerequisite_of` edges, deduping against what already exists. (5) Create the `research` entity that `investigates` the question and `explored` the sources, write its conclusion and confidence, and set the question's status to answered. Every write is proposal-gated and reviewable.
